pages.quiz:
AGRICULTURE — MOCK EXAM #20
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What word describes manure made from once-living things? (1 mark)
   A. Mineral only
   B. Plastic
   C. Organic
   D. Metal

2. Which is a benefit of drip irrigation? (1 mark)
   A. Water is wasted
   B. Fewer weeds grow between plants
   C. The leaves get very wet
   D. More weeds grow

3. Why should the holes in a drip pipe be tiny? (1 mark)
   A. So water pours out fast
   B. So the water is warm
   C. So water drips slowly
   D. So the pipe becomes lighter

4. Why is a cloth placed over the opening of the water container? (1 mark)
   A. To make the water hot
   B. To make the container heavier
   C. To colour the water
   D. To keep dirt from blocking the small holes

5. Which is a benefit of using less fuel? (1 mark)
   A. The family saves money
   B. More smoke is made
   C. The family spends more
   D. More trees must be cut

6. Which is the best material for stuffing a scarecrow? (1 mark)
   A. Stones
   B. Glass
   C. Wet mud
   D. Dry grass

7. How long may carrot seeds take to sprout? (1 mark)
   A. One day
   B. One year
   C. One hour
   D. One to three weeks

8. When should the grass mulch be removed? (1 mark)
   A. At sowing
   B. After harvesting
   C. When seedlings begin to appear
   D. Never

9. What does sowing mean? (1 mark)
   A. Putting seeds into the soil so they can grow
   B. Cutting a crop
   C. Storing seeds
   D. Watering a crop

10. About how far apart should carrot plants be after thinning? (1 mark)
   A. Touching each other
   B. 5 metres
   C. About 5 cm
   D. About 1 mm

11. Why is compost mixed into the planting hole? (1 mark)
   A. It prevents growth
   B. It makes the hole shallow
   C. It feeds the young plant and improves the soil
   D. It kills the seedling

12. Which of these completes the farm cycle: animals, manure, ____? (1 mark)
   A. Crops
   B. Roads
   C. Bricks
   D. Machines

13. Why should a poultry house be clean and dry? (1 mark)
   A. To attract rats
   B. To make eggs blue
   C. To keep birds healthy and safe
   D. To stop hens from laying

14. Which animal is kept mainly for wool? (1 mark)
   A. Wool sheep
   B. Donkey
   C. Goat
   D. Hen

15. Which of these belongs to more than one group? (1 mark)
   A. Water
   B. Groundnuts
   C. Sugar
   D. Salt

16. Which food is a good source of protein and cheap in many homes? (1 mark)
   A. Salt
   B. Beans
   C. Sugar
   D. Soda

17. Which nutrient do body-building foods supply? (1 mark)
   A. Salt
   B. Fibre only
   C. Water
   D. Protein

18. Which meal is missing protective foods? (1 mark)
   A. Ugali, beans and cabbage
   B. Sweet potato, egg and spinach
   C. Githeri and avocado
   D. Rice and fish only

19. About how long are eggs boiled for hard-boiled eggs? (1 mark)
   A. About 10 seconds
   B. About 10 minutes
   C. About 5 hours
   D. One second

20. Which of these is a kitchen safety rule? (1 mark)
   A. Use wet cloths
   B. Never leave cooking food alone
   C. Play around the stove
   D. Leave water near hot oil

21. Why should potatoes be cut into pieces of equal size before boiling? (1 mark)
   A. To make them bigger
   B. To make them cold
   C. To waste time
   D. They cook at the same time

22. Which food is cooked by deep frying and not shallow frying? (1 mark)
   A. Mandazi
   B. A fried egg
   C. Fish pieces in a pan
   D. Chapati in a pan

23. Why should you wash hands after removing gloves? (1 mark)
   A. Hands may still have germs
   B. Gloves are heavy
   C. To dry the gloves
   D. Gloves are wet

24. Which refuse can be put in the compost heap? (1 mark)
   A. Tins
   B. Plastic bottles
   C. Batteries
   D. Vegetable peelings

25. What is the first step in cleaning gumboots? (1 mark)
   A. Dry them in strong sun
   B. Put them in the fire
   C. Store them wet
   D. Knock off lumps of mud outside

26. In even tacking, the stitches and gaps are (1 mark)
   A. Absent
   B. The same length
   C. Different lengths
   D. Very long

27. What should you do with tacking when permanent sewing is done? (1 mark)
   A. Wash it
   B. Dye it
   C. Leave it for ever
   D. Cut and pull it out

28. About how long is each stitch in even tacking in this lesson? (1 mark)
   A. 10 cm
   B. 1 mm
   C. 1 metre
   D. 1 cm

29. What is one purpose of tacking? (1 mark)
   A. To hold layers of cloth together before sewing
   B. To iron cloth
   C. To cut cloth
   D. To wash cloth

30. Which thread colour is best for tacking? (1 mark)
   A. One matching the cloth exactly
   B. One that shows clearly on the cloth
   C. Black on black
   D. White on white

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Give three ways of saving fuel when cooking. (3 marks)

32. Explain what drip irrigation is. (2 marks)

33. Explain why we must not leave a fire burning after cooking. (2 marks)

34. Describe how to boil eggs. (4 marks)

35. Describe how to clean gumboots. (4 marks)

36. Describe how a family can plant trees to help conserve fuel. (4 marks)

37. Give three benefits of eating a balanced meal. (3 marks)

38. Explain why drip irrigation is useful in a dry area and describe how a school could set up a system for a row of kale. (5 marks)

39. List three materials that can be used to make a scarecrow. (3 marks)

40. List the tools and materials needed for tacking. (3 marks)

41. Explain what is wrong with a meal of ugali and salt only, and how to improve it. (3 marks)

42. Name the young of a cow, a goat and a sheep. (3 marks)

43. Explain what is meant by direct sowing. (2 marks)

44. Describe how to make even tacking. (4 marks)

45. Sila has a millet field where birds eat the grain every morning. Suggest and explain a plan to protect the crop without killing the birds. (5 marks)
pages.answers:
AGRICULTURE — MOCK EXAM #20 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — Organic
   Organic means it comes from plants and animals.

2. B — Fewer weeds grow between plants
   The soil between plants stays dry so fewer weeds grow.

3. C — So water drips slowly
   Small holes give slow drips that soak into the soil.

4. D — To keep dirt from blocking the small holes
   Dirt would clog the tiny holes.

5. A — The family saves money
   Buying less fuel means spending less.

6. D — Dry grass
   Dry grass is light and easy to use.

7. D — One to three weeks
   Carrot seeds are slow, so be patient.

8. C — When seedlings begin to appear
   Seedlings need light.

9. A — Putting seeds into the soil so they can grow
   Sowing is planting seeds.

10. C — About 5 cm
   Carrots need a few centimetres to grow roots.

11. C — It feeds the young plant and improves the soil
   Compost gives food and helps water retention.

12. A — Crops
   Manure feeds crops, and crops feed animals.

13. C — To keep birds healthy and safe
   Dirty houses spread diseases.

14. A — Wool sheep
   Some sheep breeds have wool.

15. B — Groundnuts
   Groundnuts give protein and energy.

16. B — Beans
   Beans are protein-rich.

17. D — Protein
   Protein builds muscles.

18. D — Rice and fish only
   Rice and fish have energy and protein but no vegetables or fruits.

19. B — About 10 minutes
   Ten minutes of gentle boiling makes hard eggs.

20. B — Never leave cooking food alone
   Careful supervision prevents fires.

21. D — They cook at the same time
   Equal pieces cook evenly.

22. A — Mandazi
   Mandazi float in deep oil.

23. A — Hands may still have germs
   Germs can get on hands.

24. D — Vegetable peelings
   Organic waste rots.

25. D — Knock off lumps of mud outside
   This removes the dirt before washing.

26. B — The same length
   Even tacking is equal.

27. D — Cut and pull it out
   Tacking is temporary.

28. D — 1 cm
   Even tacking uses 1 cm stitches and gaps.

29. A — To hold layers of cloth together before sewing
   Tacking keeps layers in place.

30. B — One that shows clearly on the cloth
   It is easy to see and pull out.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: Use a lid on the pot, cut food small, use dry firewood, put out the fire after cooking, soak beans first, or use an improved jiko (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.

32. (2 marks)
   Answer: It is watering plants slowly, drop by drop, next to their roots.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for slowly or drop by drop, 1 mark for near the roots.

33. (2 marks)
   Answer: It wastes fuel and can cause a fire or accident.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for waste, 1 mark for danger.

34. (4 marks)
   Answer: Put eggs in a pot, cover with cold water, bring to the boil, boil gently for about 10 minutes, cool in cold water and peel.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four steps.

35. (4 marks)
   Answer: Knock off lumps of mud; rinse; scrub with a soft brush and soapy water inside and outside; rinse again; dry upside down in the shade.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four steps.

36. (4 marks)
   Answer: Plant fast growing trees on their land for firewood, care for them and replace any tree cut with more new trees, so wood is always available and forests are not cut.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for planting, caring, replacing and result.

37. (3 marks)
   Answer: It gives energy, helps the body to grow and repair, and protects from illness.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each benefit.

38. (5 marks)
   Answer: It saves scarce water because water reaches roots directly and little is lost. For kale: raise a bucket on a stand, attach a hose along the row, close the end, ask an adult to make small holes beside each plant, fill with clean water and check that drips are slow.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for reasons, 3 marks for set-up steps.

39. (3 marks)
   Answer: Sticks or poles, old clothes, a sack, dry grass, string, tins, old CDs (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct material.

40. (3 marks)
   Answer: Needle, thread, scissors, ruler or tape measure, chalk, pins, cloth, thimble (any correct materials).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each, up to 3.

41. (3 marks)
   Answer: It only gives energy. Add beans or fish for body-building and vegetables or fruit for protective foods.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for problem, 1 for protein addition, 1 for protective addition.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Calf, kid and lamb.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct name.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: Sowing seeds straight into the place where the crop will grow until harvest.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for sowing seeds where the crop stays, 1 mark for no transplanting.

44. (4 marks)
   Answer: Mark a line; bring the needle up; make 1 cm stitches with 1 cm gaps along the line; keep the thread loose; finish with a small back stitch.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four steps.

45. (5 marks)
   Answer: Make a scarecrow with tins and shiny strips, place it in the field, move it every few days, and use a net or a noise maker. Avoid poison because it harms other living things.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for scarecrow and moving it, 1 mark for another method, 1 mark for avoiding poison, 1 mark for reason.
